masks.nondelay: admissible when the processing start is within half an hour of the earliest processing start over the compatible pairs (the rule of the paper)
masks.block: admissible when the block start (after the push past outages, before the setup) is within half an hour of the earliest block start over the compatible pairs (classical non-delay on block starts)
masks.active: admissible when the processing start is earlier than the earliest completion over the compatible pairs by more than half an hour (Giffler-Thompson)

diff: 100 (best_X - best_nondelay) / best_nondelay per case; negative means mask X gives the shorter schedules
bootstrap: P107.boot: stats_family.instance_boot, 20000 resamples, fresh default_rng(7) per quantity; pooled, a drawn instance brings its eight combinations
direction: shorter when the interval lies below zero, longer when it lies above zero, neither otherwise (the first-named mask against nondelay)
choice: the mask with the shorter best-rule schedules from the pooled direction of active against nondelay (shorter: active, longer: nondelay, neither: none); same when it is the mask the benchmark uses (mask_mode of the policy run), different otherwise
test_macro_family: Mrul (manuscript/macros_maskrule.tex): MrulDiff<Act|Blk>BestRule[Lo|Hi]<Ten|Pub>All for the pooled rows, <combination> in place of All per combination
rollouts: P107.rule_rollout (common_utils.masked_rule_action after np.random.seed(50)) with P107.make_env (exact mask options), P107.check_schedule (validator of p101) after every rollout

factory.text: factory benchmark, training size (10 modules, 25 stations)

timing.note: planning figures only; the rollouts are deterministic
